name: Other fermented milk (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Other fermented milk [Milk and milk products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 171256 - Milk, buttermilk, fluid, cultured, lowfat (NDB 01088), full nutrient/amino-acid/fatty-acid panel
Kim et al. 2019, Comprehensive Evaluation of Commercial Drinking Yogurts in Korea, PMC6837898 - organic acids (lactate/citrate/acetate) and residual sugars
Adhikari & Nilsson (Lund University) 2017, Lactose, glucose and galactose content in milk, fermented milk and lactose-free milk products, Int Dairy J doi:10.1016/j.idairyj.2017.06.005
Alm 1982, Effect of Fermentation on Lactose, Glucose, and Galactose Content in Milk, J Dairy Sci 65:346 doi:10.3168/jds.S0022-0302(82)82198-X
McCance & Widdowson / EFSA dairy references - iodine and biotin content
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources are lactic acid (the defining fermentation product, ~0.6-1.8 g/100g) plus residual lactose (~4 g/100g) and accumulating free D-galactose (~1 g/100g); free glucose is largely consumed. The database record lacked ALL organic acids and any specific-sugar breakdown - these were the main gaps and were added quantitatively. Values represent a plain unsweetened fermented milk (soured milk/kefir/cultured-buttermilk type); sweetened/flavoured drinking yogurts carry added su
curation_added: lactic acid (dominant fermentation product - was entirely absent)
lactose with a quantitative residual amount

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: Plant furanocoumarin (from Apiaceae); biologically implausible in fermented milk - FooDB predicted/expected, not measured

curation_removed.name: epsilon-Polylysine
curation_removed.reason: Manufactured microbial-derived preservative additive, not a native nutrient of fermented milk

curation_removed.name: (E)-2-Phenyl-2-butenal
curation_removed.reason: Trace aroma volatile, not a quantitatively meaningful growth nutrient

curation_removed.name: (±)-erythro-Isoleucine
curation_removed.reason: Stereoisomer artifact / duplicate of L-isoleucine; not a distinct nutrient pool

curation_removed.name: Nonanoate (nonanoic acid, C9:0)
curation_removed.reason: Odd-chain C9 acid is not a characteristic milk fatty acid at nutrient level; FooDB trace/noise

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: Free cobalt ion is a non-nutritive ultratrace; biologically relevant cobalt is supplied by vitamin B12

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: Non-nutritive trace contaminant, not a growth nutrient of milk

curation_removed.name: Chromium
curation_removed.reason: Non-nutritive ultratrace element, not characteristic of the milk matrix

composition_provenance.definition: sourced = the cited source states this component; derived = the pipeline supplied it. Classification table: tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv.

components.name: lactic acid
components.evidence_source: Kim et al. 2019 commercial drinking yogurt survey, PMC6837898 (lactate mean 767.67 mg/100g); FIL/IDF & Codex fermented-milk standard (0.6-1.8% titratable acidity as lactic acid)

components.name: citric acid
components.evidence_source: Kim et al. 2019, PMC6837898 (citrate mean 170.91 mg/100g, range 137-215)

components.name: acetic acid
components.evidence_source: Kim et al. 2019, PMC6837898 (acetate mean 31.92 mg/100g, range 18-43)

components.name: lactose
components.evidence_source: Alm 1982 J Dairy Sci 65:346 doi:10.3168/jds.S0022-0302(82)82198-X (buttermilk/kefir/ropy milk 20-30% lactose reduction from 4.8 g/100g); USDA FDC 171256 cultured lowfat buttermilk (total sugars 5.4 g)

components.name: D-galactose
components.evidence_source: Adhikari/Nilsson (Lund) 2017 Int Dairy J doi:10.1016/j.idairyj.2017.06.005; Alm 1982 doi:10.3168/jds.S0022-0302(82)82198-X (free galactose rises from traces to ~1.3 g/100g in yogurt)

components.name: D-glucose

basis: per 100 g (approx. per 100 mL; density ~1.03 g/mL) of plain unsweetened fermented/cultured milk (soured milk / kefir / cultured buttermilk type)

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
